 Hong Kong Open: Kidambi Plays Kingmaker
 Wednesday, November 18, 2026
 TEXT BY PREM KUMAR | TAN EN EN/BADMINTONPHOTO 
 SHARE 
 Kidambi Srikanth played ultimate kingmaker at LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 on Wednesday, pulling off a 21-16 16-21 21-9 surprise over Koki Watanabe to officially conclude the men’s singles Race to Finals.
 Depending on results this week, a deep run from Watanabe could have denied Kidambi’s compatriot Lakshya Sen, Chou Tien Chen or Kunlavut Vitidsarn a coveted ticket to Hangzhou. Instead, Kidambi intervened – sealing victory in 51 minutes to avenge a straight-games loss to the Japanese shuttler just last week at the Kumamoto Masters.
 The win came as a relief for Chou in particular, who had suffered a 19-21 21-7 21-19 defeat to rising Indonesian Moh Zaki Ubaidillah moments earlier. Sen had also survived a heart-stopping battle with Frenchman Arnaud Merkle 14- 21 21-16 25-23 while Vitidsarn beat Shogo Ogawa 21-7 23-21.
 While Kidambi closed the door on the men’s singles race, several players in other disciplines kept their own HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026 hopes alive by clearing their opening hurdles.
 In mixed doubles, Sapsiree Taerattanachai and Pakkapon Teeraratsakul wasted little time dispatching Canadian duo Jonathan Lai/Crystal Lai 21-13 21-12. With compatriots Dechapol Puavaranukroh and Supissara Paewsampran still in the race despite a 21-18 21-13 loss to Dejan Ferdinansyah/Felisha Alberta Nathaniel Pasaribu, the regional traffic jam has become intense.
 The Thais are now locked in a tense five-way tussle alongside tandems from neighbouring Malaysia – Goh Soon Huat/Shevon Jemie Lai and Hoo Pang Ron/Lai Pei Jing – plus Japan’s Yuta Watanabe/Maya Taguchi, all of whom also advanced on Wednesday.
 “We just try our best and keep winning as much as we can,” said Taerattanachai, acknowledging her fate is not entirely in her hands. “We know we can still make the cut but we must pray for our rivals to lose. All we can do is keep going until the end.”
 Meanwhile, in women’s singles, Putri Kusuma Wardani is fighting to secure back-to-back Finals appearances after making her debut last year. Facing Letshanaa Karupathevan, Wardani overcame a first-game wobble to triumph 21-15 21-12.
 Her path to qualification remains a dogfight against Thai contenders Ratchanok Intanon and Pornpawee Chochuwong, who both kept pace in the first round – Chochuwong outclassing Line Hojmark Kjaersfeldt 21-11 21-11 and Intanon cruising past Peng Yu Wei 21-17 21-12.
 As the final qualifying event, the stakes at the Kai Tak Arena couldn’t be higher, yet 2024 Hong Kong Open runner-up Wardani is choosing freedom over fear.
 “Since this is the last World Tour tournament counting towards Hangzhou and the fact I had a good result here, there’s a bit of pressure,” she admitted. “But I don’t want to think too far ahead; just play with a ‘nothing to lose’ mindset every match.”

 WHAT OTHERS SAID 
 “We celebrated a bit yesterday evening with some good music. It’s a huge achievement. We started the season as world No.27s and now we’ve qualified among the best eight pairs. We are really, really proud of ourselves.” – Daniel Lungaard, who yesterday qualified alongside Mads Vestergaard for their maiden Finals without lifting a racket
 “My friends and family came to support me every year only to see me lose. Finally I played a satisfactory match in front of them. I’m really relieved right now.” – Ng Ka Long Angus on winning his first Hong Kong Open match since 2017
 Vestergaard and Lungaard are Hangzhou bound.
